text:
jane.d: Quick heads up — on staging I repro a divergence between q8_0 and q2_k when doing long-doc summarization with overlapping priming sessions. Looks like KV state is drifting after ~6k tokens.
max_wu: can you paste the minimal repro?
jane.d: yep. run this against staging model-id: redwood-magnet-13b-q2_k with two concurrent clients: 
```
# spawn two clients
python tools/repro_multi_client.py --model redwood-magnet-13b-q2_k --prompt-file long_article.txt --concurrency 2 --max-tokens 8000
```
jane.d: sample stderr from the server (trimmed):
```
[2026-04-12T14:22:10Z] client=client-7 INFO prefill_len=128 kv_index=8192
[2026-04-12T14:22:15Z] client=client-3 WARN kv_index_mismatch expected=8192 got=8189
[2026-04-12T14:22:15Z] client=client-3 ERROR rope_anchor_misaligned token_pos=6123 phase_shift=3
```
liam: interesting — that kv_index_mismatch smells like anchor collision when two sessions reuse the same priming window and our RoPE offset calculation is non-idempotent across concurrent prefill flows.
liam: did you try single-client run?
jane.d: single-client stable, no mismatch. Multi-client triggers ~1/50 runs.
eva: could also be quant rounding interacting with the rotation math on q2_k. Q2_K does funny packing; a small phase offset might push interpolation into overflow territory.
max_wu: can you bisect whether this is RoPE or the KV transport? Try forcing no-rotation path in runtime and re-run.
jane.d: yes ran that — when forcing rotation-disabled (dev flag runtime::rotary_skip=true) the mismatch disappears. So points to rotation math + quant combo.
liam: good repro. assign: jane take a failing trace, max run a numerical diff between q2_k and float32 for the rotary kernel, eva run the same script with tfp-style fixed-point check.
jane.d: pushing trace to /staging/traces/1729998881/ (private link) — contains two client traces, stack info, and the kv index dump.
max_wu: posted a small probe that prints per-layer rotation scale: 
```
# quick probe
python -c "from runtime import inspect_rotary; print(inspect_rotary(model='magnet-13b-q2_k', token_pos=6000))"
```
max_wu: output shows layer2 scale differs by ~1.000003 vs float32 baseline. Not huge but multiplied over layers it accumulates.
eva: also noticed that our prefix-eviction path for concurrent sessions does a micro-shift in token_idx assignment when two prefill streams complete in the same timeslice. That could produce a 3-token phase offset.
ops-bot: @jane.d triggered job compute-daily-debug-1729998881 on worker-staging-3 :white_check_mark:
jane.d: thanks. next steps: 1) reproduce deterministically with single-process interleaved clients (I'll try a single-threaded event loop) 2) max run high-precision patch on rotary kernel 3) eva check quant packing boundary conditions and add guard for rotation wrap.
liam: also add a flaky-test that runs the two-client loop 200x under CI to catch regressions.
max_wu: on the numerical side, I'll try using int32 accumulator for rotation multiply to see if that kills the drift.
eva: if we can confirm it's the quantized rotation math, we'll add a runtime fallback: if phase_shift > 1 token then fallback to float32 for that layer. Cheap and safe.
jane.d: noted. I'll collect traces and open a short PR with failing trace + test. tagging @eng-ml for visibility. :eyes:
max_wu: ack. thanks for the quick repro, jane.
liam: ping me once you have repro + PR and I'll help bisect layers.
jane.d: will do — updating thread when I have the deterministic run.
max_wu: quick tip: include the per-client kv fingerprint and the prefill completion timestamp in trace, helps correlate race windows.
jane.d: good call, added it.
eva: nice work team. if this is real we need to block q2_k rollout on Dedicated until we have a fix or fallback.
jane.d: agreed. I'll escalate to Product if we get a clean repro. :warning:
